title: The Portrait of Windrow House
premise: True-crime podcaster Oscar Voss is hired by a nervous, wealthy client named Edith Windrow to prove that her brother's murder — scheduled, she insists — has not yet happened. Digging into the 40-year-old Windrow House case file, Oscar realizes the original investigation was steered by someone inside it, and that the 'future' murder Edith fears is a ritual replay of the old one, timed to the house's anniversary. As Oscar and their ragtag found family of researchers move into Windrow House to catch the killer in the act, they discover Edith herself is both victim and architect of the plan, and that the killer is the retired detective who closed the case. In a candlelit confrontation on the anniversary night, Oscar chooses justice outside the law — recording a confession instead of calling the police too soon — and the found family claims the house as their own studio and sanctuary.
about_author: Felix Vane is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent fifteen years transcribing testimony before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about people the system failed, from a farmhouse full of rescued animals.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid for Nothing
chapters.summary: Oscar Voss, POV. A retainer arrives with no crime attached: prove a murder hasn't happened yet. Oscar, broke after a defamation scare killed their podcast, takes the money against instinct. The beat is wary curiosity — the smell of a story that shouldn't exist.

chapters.title: Windrow House, Empty Since '84
chapters.summary: Oscar visits the decaying estate and meets Edith Windrow, who speaks of her brother's death in the future tense. POV alternates briefly with Edith's letters. Emotional beat: dread dressed as eccentricity; Oscar can't tell if she's mad or precise.

chapters.title: The File That Reads Itself
chapters.summary: Oscar's researcher Priya obtains the original case file and finds annotations no investigator should have made — corrections in the margin, dated years later. POV: Priya. Beat: the thrill of an anomaly curdling into fear that someone is watching them read.

chapters.title: Forty Years of Anniversaries
chapters.summary: Oscar maps cold cases across four decades: every anniversary, someone connected to Windrow House died identically. POV: Oscar, narrating podcast-style. Beat: vertigo — the pattern was always there, waiting for someone patient enough to see it.

chapters.title: The Detective Who Closed It
chapters.summary: Oscar interviews retired Inspector Hale, charming and helpful, who offers the file's 'real' answer too readily. POV: Oscar. Beat: unease beneath politeness; Hale knows details never made public, and Oscar pretends not to notice.

chapters.title: Moving In
chapters.summary: The team — Oscar, Priya, sound engineer Dev, and ex-cop Marisol — moves into Windrow House under cover of restoration. POV: Dev. Beat: tentative warmth, the found family joking through fear as they wire every room with microphones.

chapters.title: Edith's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: Edith nearly tells Oscar something crucial, then retreats into talk of her brother's portrait, which hangs crooked no matter how often it's straightened. POV: Oscar. Beat: tenderness and frustration — she wants to be saved but only by someone who understands first.

chapters.title: The Second Body
chapters.summary: A groundskeeper connected to the house dies exactly as the pattern predicts — ruled accidental. POV: Marisol, whose cop instincts scream murder while local police wave her off. Beat: grief and rage; the clock is real now.

chapters.title: What the Portrait Hides
chapters.summary: Behind the brother's portrait, Oscar finds Edith's decades of surveillance notes on Hale — she has suspected him since 1984. POV: Oscar. Beat: revelation and horror; the client hired them to confirm what she already knew.

chapters.title: Hale Comes to Dinner
chapters.summary: Hale visits the house uninvited, probing the team's presence with friendly menace. POV: Dev, mic'd and terrified, capturing everything. Beat: a duel conducted entirely in pleasantries; the family closes ranks around Oscar.

chapters.title: Priya Disappears
chapters.summary: Priya goes missing after pulling Hale's personnel records. POV: alternating Oscar and Priya, held somewhere with a radio playing the podcast. Beat: terror and guilt — Oscar's show may have led the killer straight to her.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath the Stairs
chapters.summary: Marisol finds a hidden room: forty years of trophies, each anniversary death documented in Hale's hand. POV: Marisol. Beat: cold clarity — this is bigger than one killer; it's a career built on unsolved cases.

chapters.title: The Trap We Set Ourselves
chapters.summary: The team debates: go to police and lose everything to jurisdiction and Hale's old boys, or stay and spring the trap themselves. POV: Oscar. Beat: the theme crystallizes — duty says call, justice says stay; love for Priya tips the scale.

chapters.title: Anniversary Eve
chapters.summary: The house prepared like a stage set; Edith dresses as she did in 1984. POV: Edith, finally. Beat: quiet courage — she has waited forty years to be bait, and she is not afraid anymore.

chapters.title: The Replay Begins
chapters.summary: Hale enters the house at midnight, following the script of the original murder. Hidden mics carry his movements through the walls. POV: Dev at the soundboard. Beat: unbearable suspense — everyone listening, no one allowed to breathe.

chapters.title: Confession in Candlelight
chapters.summary: In the portrait room, Hale explains the murders to Edith as a kind of devotion — keeping the case perfect, forever his. Oscar steps out of the dark, recording. POV: Oscar. Beat: triumph laced with revulsion at how much he loved his own work.

chapters.title: The Choice With the Knife
chapters.summary: Hale takes Edith hostage; police are twenty minutes out. Oscar must stall using the one thing Hale respects — the case file itself, reciting his own crimes back to him. POV: Oscar. Beat: love against duty made literal; words as weapons.

chapters.title: What Marisol Did
chapters.summary: Marisol breaks protocol and takes Hale down hard, off the record, before the sirens arrive. POV: Marisol. Beat: catharsis and cost — she may have ended her chance at redemption, and doesn't regret it.

chapters.title: After the Tape Stops
chapters.summary: Fallout: the recording is admissible enough, Hale is charged, and the podcast explodes. But Oscar sits with the ethics of what they did. POV: Oscar. Beat: hollow victory; justice outside the law still leaves bruises.

chapters.title: Edith's Last Portrait
chapters.summary: Edith, dying peacefully, asks Oscar to hang the portrait straight at last — and leaves the house to the team. POV: Edith. Beat: release; she finally gets the ending the system never gave her brother.

chapters.title: The Family That Stayed
chapters.summary: The team converts Windrow House into a studio for investigating the forgotten dead. Small scenes of domestic warmth: Dev's equipment in the ballroom, Priya's archive in the hidden room. POV: rotating ensemble. Beat: found family made permanent.

chapters.title: One More Letter
chapters.summary: Months later, a letter arrives: another impossible request, another case that hasn't happened yet. Oscar smiles, hits record. POV: Oscar. Beat: the loop reopens — sequel-ready, but complete; they are no longer invisible, and neither are the victims.
